paragraphs.text: Branchpoint for DeepSeek Harness: fork the current chat into a fresh branch with a compact digest.
# Branchpoint
**Fork the conversation at a clean point.**
Branchpoint is a DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin that adds a fork button to the chat header. Click it
and Branchpoint lists the sections it can split off — a practice set, a theory topic, a single formu
la or code fragment, or the whole branch. Pick one and it opens a fresh session with only that secti
on's digest already in the composer.
Long chats degrade. Compaction helps, but it also blurs the thread. Branchpoint gives you a clean br
anch that still knows where you were.
## What it does

- Adds a fork icon to `conversation.session.header.actions`, next to the branch title.
- Loads up to

six older pages of session history when the prompt is outside the current window.
- Auto-detects sp

littable units in the branch:
- sections with numbered tasks («Практика 2», «Задания», «Упражнения»)
pens a picker: task sections first with their task count, then theory sections, then **«Разобрать»**
— formulas, functions, code fragments and libraries that matter but are not the topic itself. Each

row has a one-line preview.
- Builds a scoped digest for the chosen unit:
- the topic name from the

first real request;
- only that section's numbered tasks/questions — no other sections, no context b

lock;
- formulas stay in their original LaTeX (`$\log_2 32$`), so DSH renders them with KaTeX exactl
y as in the main branch; the readable form (`log₂(32)`) is used only for one-line previews in the pi

d full summary: goal, all topics, all tasks/questions, conclusion, done/open, files and commands.
-
Opens a new session and puts the digest in the draft. It does **not** send automatically, so you can

review it first.
- Numbers branches per parent: the digest starts with `🌿 Ветка 1 · …`, `🌿 Ветка 2
· …`, so the left panel never shows two identical branch titles. The root chat is renamed `🌳 …` and

pinned once, so the main branch stays visible above its branches.
- Remembers the parent session. A
branch gets a **↩** button that opens the main branch with a short note in its composer: «задания вы
полнены», «вопрос разобран», or the result and changed files for a code branch.
## Example digest
[代码示例省略，未执行]
### Topic branches
Branchpoint splits a structured lesson or project chat by its Markdown sections. A section with at l
east two numbered items under a task-like heading becomes a **task unit**; other sections with enoug
h text become **theory units**. Selecting a unit creates a branch that knows only that part.
Example: the main chat has «Практика 2» after a change-of-base explanation. The picker shows «Практи
ка 2 — 7 заданий». The new branch gets only this:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Formulas keep their original LaTeX, so the branch renders them with KaTeX exactly like the main chat
. The picker still shows a readable preview (`log₄(8)`) because its rows are one line of plain text.
## How it works

- `lib/index.js` is a minimal host half (`name`, empty `apply`).
- `lib/client.js`:
- `inject = ['sl

x.sessions.binding(sessionId).eventSource`;
- `entriesToTurns` and `entriesToTools` parse messages a
assistant answers into Markdown or bold headings (ignoring headings inside code fences) and detects
numbered task blocks; `collectConcepts` finds formulas, functions, code fragments and imported libr

aries;
- `buildUnitDigest` renders only the chosen section and keeps formulas as original LaTeX; `re
adableMath` is used only for one-line picker previews; `buildDigest` still renders the full branch;

- the picker is a React portal (`react-dom`) with Escape/backdrop close;
- `createBranch` uses `ctx.

uiWorkspace.openWorkspace` to capture the new session id and `prepareDraft` to fill its composer;
-
`nextBranchNumber` numbers branches per parent; `markMain` renames the root chat to `🌳 …` once and p

ins it;
- the parent id and unit metadata are stored in `localStorage`; `returnToMain` opens the par
ent and prepares `buildReturnNote` as a draft.
No build step: `lib/client.js` is a ready ESM bundle in the `window.__ModuleLoader__` envelope.
## Limitations
- The digest is built from the **DSH session event log**. Reasoning and raw tool output are not summ

arized; only visible assistant text, tool errors, changed files and commands are used.
- The digest
framing is English. Quoted conclusions stay in the language of the chat, since they are extracted ve

rbatim.
- Section detection relies on Markdown headings (`## …`), bold headings (`**…**`), and numbe

red lists (`1. …`). A plain-prose chat may show no section rows; «Вся ветка» still works.
- A task s

ection needs at least two numbered items; a theory section needs at least 160 characters.
- Formulas
stay as LaTeX in the digest, so the branch renders them like the main chat after the message is sen

t. The composer itself is plain text: until you send, `$\log_2 32$` is visible as source.
- Branch n
umbers count only branches created by 0.6.0 or later for that parent; older branches keep their titl

es and do not consume a number.
- The **↩** button appears only for branches created by 0.5.0 or lat

er, and only while the browser keeps the `localStorage` link.
- The tree mark and pin are applied on
ce to the root chat when you first split a branch from it. If the chat is unnamed (no visible title

yet), the mark is retried on the next branch.
- The return note replaces any unsent draft in the mai

n composer.
- History is paged at most six times per click, so extremely long sessions may still nee

d a second click to reach the original prompt.
- If a branch has no assistant text and no tool resul
ts, Branchpoint shows an alert and does not open an empty session.
